edition.notes: The edition reprints the Verona editors' text with Migne's prefatory and column apparatus. The prologue begins at PL 26 col. 15; the Lukan provenance sentence appears at col. 18.
edition.publication: Domenico Vallarsi and Scipione Maffei editorial text, reprinted in Jacques-Paul Migne, Patrologia Latina 26 (Paris, 1845), cols. 15-218
edition.title: Commentariorum in Evangelium Matthaei ad Eusebium libri quattuor, Vallarsi text reprinted in Patrologia Latina 26

passages.context: In his prologue's ordered account of the four canonical evangelists, Jerome identifies Luke as a physician, a Syrian of Antioch, and a disciple of Paul, and says that Luke composed his volume in the regions of Achaia and Boeotia. This controls attribution of that Achaia-Boeotia provenance as Jerome's ancient testimony, not as an independently demonstrated modern historical conclusion.
passages.notes: Directly inspected at PL 26 col. 18, artifact PDF p. 14. The adjacent Vallarsi note reports contrary ancient testimony and the Syriac version's Egypt/Alexandria claim; this passage therefore supports faithful reporting of Jerome's attribution while preserving the edition's visible disagreement. It does not establish a precise city, year, manuscript stemma, or modern critical consensus.

work.author: Jerome
work.description: Jerome's four-book commentary on Matthew, preceded by a prologue that situates each canonical evangelist and explains the fourfold Gospel.
work.title: Commentariorum in Evangelium Matthaei ad Eusebium libri quattuor
